_comment: Disposable-implant insertion routes. The list resolves entries by ROW NAME, so each route gets its own name and is registered as a real passive with the target's display name and Rank -- that is what makes it render correctly where a bare duplicate row showed placeholder text. PassiveSkill deliberately points at the ALIAS, not the real passive: pointing it at the real one would make BP_FindRowByPassiveSkill ambiguous and could report this 1000g price for the recipe route. The alias has no effects of its own; main.lua swaps it for the real passive as soon as the vanilla transaction installs it. This file is hand-maintained and is the source of truth for these 54 routes; each row's Rank is the target passive's own rank, which is what colours its entry in the list. Row order is meaningful -- the operation list is drawn in raw row order -- so add to the end rather than re-sorting. Every row here needs a matching key in lp/ids.lua's IMPLANT_TARGET: a row with no key installs an inert alias and leaves it on the Pal, and a key with no row is a dead list entry.
